articles.title: Bears get update on injured player who left practice in ‘significant discomfort’
articles.summary: Swift’s latest injury scare has the Bears watching closely with Week 1 approaching.
articles.body:
The NFL season is just around the corner, and the Chicago Bears are hoping running back D'Andre Swift's latest injury scare does not turn into a significant setback before their season opener.

Swift reportedly left Thursday's practice in "significant discomfort" while holding his midsection. The veteran running back was believed to be dealing with a cramp, providing some relief for the Bears as they await further evaluation.

Chicago is scheduled to have several days off before beginning its final preparations for the Sept. 13 opener against the Carolina Panthers. The timing gives Swift an opportunity to recover, and the Bears will be hoping the issue proves to be nothing more than a temporary problem.

Aug 22, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (4) runs the ball during the first half against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images

Swift is entering his second season with Chicago after producing another impressive campaign in 2025. He appeared in 16 regular-season games and surpassed 1,000 rushing yards for the second time in his career.

The 27-year-old averaged 4.9 yards per carry while recording nine rushing touchdowns and another score through the air. His production has made him an important part of Chicago's offense, particularly with the team looking to build on its breakthrough season.

Swift's health will therefore be something to monitor closely over the coming days. While the initial indication that he was dealing with a cramp is encouraging, the Bears cannot afford to lose another key member of their running back room.

Bears already dealing with running back injury

Chicago is already without running back Kyle Monangai, who suffered a leg injury during practice on Aug. 16. Monangai is considered week-to-week and is reportedly doubtful to play in Week 1, although initial testing suggested the injury should not result in a long-term absence.

That makes Swift's status particularly important as the Bears prepare for the regular season. Avoiding another injury at the position would give Chicago a much-needed boost heading into its title defense.

The Bears are coming off their first NFC North championship since 2018 and will enter the new season with expectations significantly higher than they have been in recent years. Keeping Swift healthy could be a key part of their hopes of returning to the postseason and making another deep run.

articles.title: How a five-month exile from NFL media may have actually made Dianna Russini more valuable than ever before
articles.summary: NFL News: Dianna Russini quietly left NFL media in April after photographs surfaced showing her with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel at an Arizona r.
articles.body: Dianna Russini quietly left NFL media in April after photographs surfaced showing her with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel at an Arizona resort. No dramatic farewell. No press tour. Just a resignation letter that insisted her reporting was solid, and a vow that this moment would not define her. Five months later, The Athletic released findings from a sweeping investigation of her entire body of work. The conclusion surprised a lot of people, and it may have just handed Russini the strongest possible card to play on her way back.What did The Athletic investigation actually find about Dianna Russini?The scope of the review was significant. Investigators combed through 903 written stories, 204 podcast episodes, 77 videos, and a range of additional appearances. After all of that, the conclusion on the journalism itself was clear: there was no meaningful evidence that Dianna Russini used her platform to favor Mike Vrabel or push his interests. Only roughly 5% of her reviewed work even involved him or teams he coached. Four pieces received recommended editor's notes, but the overwhelming body of her reporting raised no concerns.What the investigation did find was a process failure. Russini's undisclosed relationship with Vrabel was a direct violation of The Athletic's editorial standards. The review also noted that she handled early questions about the resort photographs poorly. Those are real criticisms. But they sit separately from the journalism question, and on that front, the findings were largely in her favor.For Russini, that distinction matters enormously. She did not leave sports media under a cloud of fabricated stories or compromised scoops. She left because of a personal relationship she kept hidden. That is a different conversation, and the investigation, whether intentionally or not, drew that line clearly.Where could Dianna Russini land after her NFL media comeback?According to Front Office Sports, Russini is "absolutely" planning a return and has been exploring multiple opportunities. The options reportedly range from a traditional NFL insider role to something closer to a personality or opinion-driven format. No final decision has been made.One name that keeps surfacing is Barstool Sports. Dave Portnoy has already gone on record calling hiring Russini a "no-brainer," and she has existing relationships with the Pardon My Take hosts. That kind of platform would be a genuine departure from the beat reporter lane she occupied at ESPN and The Athletic, but it might also be exactly where the audience momentum is right now.The NFL regular season opens September 9. That date is functioning as an informal deadline. Sports media moves quickly when a new season arrives, and an NFL insider without a platform during opening week is a missed opportunity nobody wants.What Russini's absence has done, somewhat counterintuitively, is create space for the market to miss her. Sources, access, institutional knowledge — those do not expire in five months. The investigation clearing the core of her work means potential employers are not taking on a liability. They are picking up an experienced reporter whose last controversy turned out to be mostly personal, not professional.The question is no longer whether Russini returns. It is where, and how quickly the NFL media world moves to make it happen.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pro Football Hall of Fame revamps selection process to combat 'unintended biases' months after Bill Belichick snub
articles.summary: The Pro Football Hall of Fame is making changes for the class of 2027.
articles.body:
Months after New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick was snubbed for the Pro Football Hall of Fame , the organization announced it would revamp its voting process moving forward. In an announcement Friday, the Hall of Fame said it would reduce its pool of voters and adjust how players are considered for induction, among other changes.

As part of those changes, the selection pool will be whittled down from 50 members to 25 members, with three other nonvoting participants taking part each year. Those members will no longer be required to come from each NFL market.

Additionally, the Hall of Fame will eliminate its senior category — which previously included players "who had their modern-era eligibility expire after 25 years," per ESPN. Instead, all players will be considered as a group. Hall of Fame candidacy will no longer expire, so older players can remain in consideration in perpetuity.

Pro Football Hall of Fame CEO Jim Porter said these changes were made after a two-and-a-half-year review of the voting process. He added that these changes will go into effect as the voters consider the class of 2027 , per ESPN.

"The Hall continually reviews its bylaws to ensure the selection process reflects the highest standards of integrity and the magnitude of election to the Pro Football Hall of Fame,'' Porter said in a statement. "There is no more important task at the Hall of Fame than the election of each new class.''

Porter added that the changes were made to prevent "unintended biases'' from leaking into the process.

That the changes come months after Belichick's snub is probably not a coincidence. As Mike Sando — who has served on the Hall of Fame selection committee since 2010 — of The Athletic detailed, a change to the voting process in 2025 may have resulted in Belichick not getting into the Hall of Fame in his first year of eligibility.

Under the previous process, the Hall of Fame lumped Belichick in a group with three senior candidates and a contributor. Instead of fast-tracking Belichick into the Hall, some voters prioritized those senior members who have been waiting for the honor, per Sando. That likely led to former San Francisco 49ers running back Roger Craig finally getting the honor, while Belichick and Patriots owner Robert Kraft were snubbed.

Under the new process, Belichick and Kraft would not be lumped in a small group with senior candidates. They would instead be considered with every other player.

Once a list of 15 individuals — 13 players, one contributor and one coach — are determined, the Hall of Fame voters will meet to whittle down that list until seven candidates are put up for induction. From there, voters will be required to vote for six of the final seven, per Sando. Only those with 80 percent of the votes will be inducted into the Pro Football of Fame.

That could lead to larger Hall of Fame class sizes moving forward, a welcome development for worthy players who kept getting pushed off the final ballot under the Hall's previous voting process.
